items.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I did my first album, I was twelve years old, under the direction of Joe Newman, Zoot Sims, Art Davis and Hank Jones

ctx.x: You see? So it’s totally different. But this is what happens. There’s a serious problem there now. There’s a serious problem within the direction of the music. The musical industry right now, the record sales have fallen fifty percent below than what they normally were. Because number one, if you record a record, I don’t care how much you write, if there’s not much experience in writing, it’s going to be the same thing. So you’ve done five albums of the same thing. The sales don’t stay here, they go there you…

accents. So if the bass player rushes, the drummer doesn’t control. He’s not in control. And everything went up a meter. And if you listen to Miles Davis “Four and More” album, right, and you listen to the ones he did with John Coltrane, it’s the same music but the tempos are double. That shows you where it started off with the younger generation. They took it from the double tempo and went on with it.
